newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-TIGER WOODS FIRES COURSE RECORD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS FIRES COURSE RECORD.

text.p: Tiger Woods, showing no signs of the heat exhaustion which laid him low two days ago, fired a course record eight-under-par 64 on Friday to take the second round lead in the Bangkok Classic.
Woods fired nine birdies and one bogey for a 10-under 134 and a two-stroke lead over Dubai-based Englishman Lee Petters, Mexico's Carlos Espinosa and American Greg Hanrahan.
"I felt a lot better today, I am over the jet lag," said Woods who was forced to pull out of the pro-am on Wednesday after the 13th hole due to heat exhaustion and jet lag.
The 21-year-old American, a local favourite because of his Thai mother, started the day two under but quickly moved up the leaderboard after playing the front nine in 32.
Petters, the first round leader who had 14 stitches inserted in his nose on Thursday after getting whacked in the face by his playing partner's driver, carded a two-under 70.
